claims.head: The Devils like Mantha’s line against Moore’s
claims.call: The Devils’ L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) spends at least 39% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Mantha’s line (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Kings’ third line is Moore, Laughton and Armia.
claims.nums: At home: 39% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 27% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · New Jersey home games this season · 7 games, 54 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: New Jersey’s L3 (Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer) at home: 39% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, New Jersey home games this season, 7 games, 54 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 27% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: The Devils’ edge in the power play
claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, and the Kings are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. These two rarely give each other power plays, so special teams may not get much of a say.

notes.text: Kevin Fiala is on injured reserve (lower-leg surgery) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Alex Turcotte is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Quinton Byfield is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Alex Laferriere has taken his spot beside Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin.

NJD.head: The matchup suits the Devils
NJD.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Los Angeles may be without Byfield. The Kings’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

LAK.head: The Kings have a hill to climb
